title: Strict-tower localization and projection realization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are separated of finite type. At $A_n$ write $\mathcal C_{T,A_n}=D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor category; at $R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ write $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$. Integral categories use completed coefficient sheaves and derived completeness with reductions in one finite cohomological interval independent of $n$; field categories use rationalization and common finite coefficient-field stages, respectively. 

Let $f:X\to Y$, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed with complementary open $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and let $K\in\mathcal C_{X,\Lambda}$. Use the counit, unit and connecting map of the open--closed recollement triangle [def-weil-open-closed-recollement]. There is a functorial distinguished triangle of the actual compact-support functor values
$$R(fj)_!j^*K\longrightarrow Rf_!K\longrightarrow R(fi)_!i^*K\longrightarrow R(fj)_!j^*K[1].$$
Its first two arrows are the images of the recollement counit and unit, identified by the canonical composition and proper-coincidence maps. At integral coefficients, for any one fixed compactification $c$ of $f$, its three vertices, all three arrows and their quotient-induced transitions are the total derived inverse limits of the strict reduction-tower image of the recollement triangle. Thus the connecting arrow is the one of this coherent tower triangle. Rationalization and exact common-stage embeddings identify this triangle with the corresponding field-stage triangles. These assertions include $U=\varnothing$ and $Z=\varnothing$ and respect Weil structures when $X,Z,U,f$ descend to the fixed finite field and the input has a Weil structure [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].
For $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ and $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ on the bounded domains above, the canonical projection map [def-exchange-projection]
$$Rf_!K\otimes^L L\longrightarrow Rf_!(K\otimes^L f^*L)$$
is an isomorphism, natural in both inputs, compatible with composition, compactification comparisons, finite reduction, finite scalar extension, and proper coincidence. The integral tensor and pullback in this formula are completed operations.
